CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in both hands.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
60-year-old right-handed male presents with numbness and tingling in both hands for a few weeks, worsening over the last month. Symptoms began after a motor vehicle accident in December with bilateral wrist fractures. On the right side, symptoms extend from the middle and ring fingers up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring fingers. Patient reports the symptoms are mainly soreness with occasional throbbing, associated with weakness, particularly when using his hands. Tingling is more prominent when pain is present and becomes dull when pain resolves. Symptoms occur mainly at night and come and go throughout the day. Denies loss of sensation but reports decreased sensitivity in hands. No significant loss of sensation noted. Patient was prescribed nerve pain medication but has not been taking it consistently. Right wrist was more severely injured than left, and patient currently wears splints on both wrists, with the right being worse.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: fatigue and weight gain. Eyes: floaters. Cardiovascular: shortness of breath and leg swelling. Gastrointestinal: excessive appetite and bloating. Endocrine: increased hunger. Skin: nail bed changes, dryness, itching. Musculoskeletal: gout and muscle pain. Remainder of review of systems is negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident in December with bilateral wrist fractures and head contusion. Hypertension. Anxiety. History of prediabetes, currently controlled with diet modification. Mild neck stiffness since motor vehicle accident.

MEDICATIONS
Coreg for hypertension. Lexapro for anxiety. Nerve pain medication (not taken consistently).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Right-handed. Motor vehicle accident in December with bilateral wrist fractures.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination: Pin prick sensation diminished in third and fourth fingers on the right. Sensation decreased in fourth and fifth fingers on the left. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ at knees; toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Rest of exam is normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, likely secondary to past wrist trauma from motor vehicle accident. Plan to schedule electromyography (EMG) test to precisely localize nerve irritation. Patient to continue wearing splints on both wrists. Will follow up after testing. If symptoms persist, will consider referral to hand clinic for possible injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedist for same treatment options.
